title: Construct Binary Tree From Preorder And Inorder Traversal
description: You are given the preorder and inorder traversals of a binary tree whose values are all unique. Rebuild the tree and return its root.
constraints: All values are unique and both arrays describe the same tree
hints: Which element of the preorder array is always the root?
Find that root in the inorder array: everything to its left is the left subtree, everything to its right is the right subtree.
Look up root positions in a value -> index map. Consume preorder with a moving pointer, building left before right, and pass inorder bounds instead of slicing.
starterCode:
class Solution:
    def buildTree(self, preorder: List[int], inorder: List[int]) -> Optional[TreeNode]:

expected.$py: [x for i in range(1,3000) for x in (i,None)]+[3000]
[3000]+[x for i in range(2999,0,-1) for x in (i,None)][:-1]

solution.explanation: The first preorder value is the root. Its position in the inorder array splits the remaining values into the left subtree (before it) and the right subtree (after it). Precompute a value -> inorder index map, keep a pointer into preorder, and recursively build the left subtree then the right subtree over inorder index ranges, so no slicing is needed. Each node is created once: O(n) time, O(n) space for the map and recursion.
